rules: UNIT CONVENTION: rate_pct is in PERCENT of purchase price per year (1.18 = 1.18%/yr). Engine must divide by 100. This intentionally matches structural.py's percent form and REPLACES data_providers.STATE_PROPERTY_TAX_RATE, which is (a) decimal-fraction form and (b) homeowner-effective — its CA 0.0075, FL 0.0091, SC 0.0057, IN 0.0084, TX 0.0180 values are all WRONG for an investor purchase and must not be blended with this table. Fallback for missing/invalid code: 1.10 (unweighted table median ~1.10). ENGINE RULES: (1) Year-1 tax = rate_pct x PURCHASE price; from the first post-renovation assessment (model as year 2+) use rate_pct x ARV, because nearly all states capture the rehab at reassessment — exceptions: OR (only 'exception value' of the remodel is added at the changed-property ratio), NV (depreciated-replacement-cost basis mutes it), AZ (LPV growth capped 5%/yr, no sale reset). (2) LTR-conditional rates baked into this table assume the BRRRR default (long-term tenant) AND timely filing: MT reduced-rate application (Dec 1–Mar 1 annually), UT primary-residential declaration, SC 25% ATI exemption by Jan 30 after purchase, NV low-income-rent 3% cap election. Flip mode: MT reverts to second-home tiers (~1.2–1.9x shown rate), UT to 1.0, and DC risks the 5% vacant / 10% blighted class mid-rehab unless the active-construction exemption is filed. (3) Known drift to encode: OH rentals +~0.1pp by TY2029 (non-business credit phase-out, HB335); TX non-homestead 20% appraisal circuit breaker expires end-2026. (4) Annual-growth caps that survive for a HOLD (bill/assessment growth, all reset at next sale): FL 10% non-homestead, NV 8% (3% low-income), IN hard ceiling 2% of AV, NM 3% (after reset year), AR 10%. (5) High-variance states where a statewide scalar is least trustworthy for metro ranking — prefer per-metro overrides: NY (0.8 NYC vs 3.3 upstate), TX, FL, PA, RI, AK, LA, HI.
notes: Method: baseline = Tax Foundation effective rates on owner-occupied housing (CY2023 ACS, published 2025), then per-state investor adjustment: (a) acquisition-value reset states set to new-purchase rate (CA 1% + local adds = 1.1–1.3; FL/OK/AR/NM/SC/MI reset or uncap at transfer); (b) classification-ratio states scaled to the investor ratio (SC 6/4 + Act 388 school millage, AL 20/10, MS 15/10, WV Class III–IV 1.5–2x, SD school-levy split, IN 2% cap, MI +18 non-PRE mills, VT non-homestead $1.703); (c) homestead/credit removal (ID 50%/$125k, LA $75k, ME $25k, TX $140k school, IN deductions, AZ rebate, ND $1,600 credit, WY 25%, OH 2.5% + rollback phase-out, NY STAR, MD/MA/RI owner programs); (d) investor-favorable carve-outs kept per BRRRR default (UT 45% exemption and MT homestead-tier rates both extend to long-term rentals). 2025–26 law changes are incorporated: MT HB231/SB542, OH HB335 rollback phase-out, SD SB121, TX Nov-2025 $140k homestead (owner-only, so it RAISES the investor-vs-owner gap), CO 2026 split ratios, VT FY26 rates, Honolulu FY2025-26 Res-A tiers. 11 entries are estimated:true where statewide investor averages required judgment (AK, AR, DE, LA, MT, NV, NM, NY, RI, SD); they are bounded by statutory structure, not guesses. Sanity anchors vs old repo table: investor rate > repo homeowner rate in every overlapping state, with the biggest deltas exactly where theory predicts (SC 0.57→1.40, IN 0.84→1.75, FL 0.91→1.50, CA 0.75→1.18 purchase-reset).

AL.basis_note: Class II rental assessed at 20% vs 10% owner-occupied Class III -> ~2x owner effective (0.36%); no homestead. Same millages.

AK.basis_note: Anchorage/Mat-Su dominate; investor loses Anchorage 20%-up-to-$75k residential exemption; Anchorage mill rates ~1.3-1.45%. Some rural boroughs levy no property tax.

AZ.basis_note: Class 4 rental = same 10% ratio as owner Class 3, but investor loses the Homeowner Rebate (state pays ~40-50% of school primary tax, cap ~$600). Limited Property Value does NOT reset on sale.

AR.basis_note: 20% ratio x ~45-50 avg mills; Amendment 79 caps reset on transfer (assessed -> full appraised); investor loses ~$500 homestead credit; county appraisals lag market.

CA.basis_note: Prop 13: reassessed to PURCHASE PRICE; 1% base + voter-approved debt = 1.1-1.3% typical (SF 1.18%, LA ~1.25%). Do NOT use the ~0.7% homeowner average. Mello-Roos extra in some subdivisions.

CO.basis_note: Same residential assessment ratio for rentals (2026: ~7.05% school / 6.8% local, 10% reduction on first $700k) x ~75 avg mills. No owner-occupant break.

CT.basis_note: 70% assessment x ~30 avg mills; no meaningful homestead (new municipal-option exemption barely adopted); investor = owner (1.92% TF 2023).

DE.basis_note: No homestead (senior school credit only); investor = owner. First countywide reassessments in ~50 years (2024-25) normalized values; rates rebalanced.

DC.basis_note: Class 1 residential $0.85/$100 of assessed (near market); investor loses homestead deduction (~$89k) and 10% assessment cap. WARNING: registered-vacant 5%/blighted 10% class during rehab unless active-construction exemption filed.

FL.basis_note: New purchase assessed near market; statewide avg ~17 mills (FL DOR). No homestead/Save Our Homes for investors; 10% non-homestead cap starts after yr 1 and RESETS at sale. Do NOT use the ~0.8% homeowner average.

GA.basis_note: 40% ratio, county millages; investor loses county/school homestead exemptions and 2025 HB581 floating homestead (owner-only). Owner eff ~0.85 -> investor ~1.0.

HI.basis_note: Honolulu Residential A (no home exemption, >$1M): 0.40% first $1M + 1.14% above; NOO under $1M: 0.35%. Maui NOO tiers higher (LTR exemption available); blended SFR investor ~0.5%. Lowest in US but 2-3x the 0.27% owner average.

ID.basis_note: Investor loses homeowner's exemption (50% of value up to $125k, ~25-30% of a median home). Owner eff 0.47 -> investor ~0.65.

IL.basis_note: Owner eff 2.07% (TF 2023) + loss of General Homestead Exemption ($6k/$10k EAV). Cook Co rentals (<=6 units) same 10% level as owner SFR. Highest-tier state.

IN.basis_note: Rentals under 2% constitutional circuit-breaker cap (vs 1% homestead); urban districts at/near the 2% cap, rural below; no homestead/supplemental deductions. Do NOT use ~0.85% homeowner avg.

IA.basis_note: Residential rollback (~47%) applies to rentals too; x ~$33/1000 avg consolidated levy. Homestead exemption small, so investor ~= owner.

KS.basis_note: 11.5% ratio x ~130 avg mills; investor loses only the $75k exemption from the 20-mill statewide school levy (trivial). Appraisals near market.

KY.basis_note: Full-value assessment; state 11.4c/$100 + local; homestead only for 65+/disabled, so investor = owner.

LA.basis_note: 10% ratio x ~110 avg mills = ~1.1% statutory; investor loses the $75k (market) homestead exemption, a huge share of modest-value homes -> ~1.8x owner eff (0.51). Parish variance is wide.

ME.basis_note: Investor loses $25k homestead exemption; otherwise same mill rates. Owner eff ~1.0.

MD.basis_note: Investor gets no Homestead assessment-growth cap or Homeowners' credit; new purchase at full phased-in assessment; state 11.2c + county (Baltimore City 2.25%).

MA.basis_note: Near-market assessments x ~$11-12/1000 avg; residential exemption (Boston ~35%, Cambridge, Somerville etc.) is owner-only so investors pay materially more in those cities.

MI.basis_note: Taxable value UNCAPS to SEV (50% of market) at transfer + rentals pay ~18 extra school operating mills (non-PRE avg ~50 mills total) -> ~2.2-2.5% of purchase. Do NOT use the ~1.3% homeowner avg.

MN.basis_note: Non-homestead SFR (4bb) class rate 1.00% <=$500k same as homestead, but loses homestead market-value exclusion (up to ~$38k) and refunds; rentals exempt from state general levy.

MS.basis_note: Class II non-owner-occupied assessed 15% vs 10% Class I owner (1.5x) + loss of homestead credit. Owner eff ~0.75 -> ~1.1.

MO.basis_note: 19% residential ratio for both; no investor/owner rate distinction (senior credit only); KC/STL metro levies above state avg.

MT.basis_note: 2025-26 reform (HB231/SB542): LONG-TERM RENTALS qualify for the reduced graduated homestead rates (0.76%/0.9%/1.1% tiers of market -> taxable, x ~550-680 mills) IF owner applies (window Dec 2025-Mar 2026, then annually). Second homes/STRs pay up to 1.9% tier (~2x).

NE.basis_note: No owner/investor distinction; LB34 school-tax credits apply to all property. Owner eff ~1.5.

NV.basis_note: 35% ratio on taxable value (land + depreciated replacement cost, 1.5%/yr up to 75% - favors older BRRRR stock); abatement resets at sale, then 8% annual bill cap for rentals (3% if rents within low-income limits).

NH.basis_note: No homestead exemption; investor = owner; town rates on near-market equalized values.

NJ.basis_note: Highest in US (owner eff 2.23% TF 2023); ANCHOR/Senior Freeze are owner rebates, not rate cuts, so investor pays full levy.

NM.basis_note: 3% annual valuation cap does NOT protect the year after a transfer (resets toward market); residential rates same for rentals; small head-of-family exemption lost.

NY.basis_note: STAR is owner-only. Massive intrastate spread: NYC Class 1 ~0.8-0.9%, Long Island ~2.1-2.3%, upstate metros (Buffalo/Rochester/Syracuse) 2.5-3.3%. Statewide blend for SFR investor ~1.95; MUST override per-metro.

NC.basis_note: No owner/investor distinction; 2025 revaluations pulled assessed toward market with partial rate rollbacks.

ND.basis_note: Investor loses the primary-residence credit ($1,600 by 2025 HB1176, owner-only); otherwise same levies on 4.5% of half... (net ~1% of market).

OH.basis_note: 35% ratio; rentals lose the 2.5% owner-occupancy credit, and the 10% non-business credit for rentals is PHASING OUT (7.5% TY2026 -> 0% TY2029, HB335) so drift +~0.1pp by 2029. Recent reappraisals jumped values.

OK.basis_note: ~11% ratio x ~90-110 mills; 5% assessment cap resets on sale (new purchase at market); homestead exemption ($1k assessed) trivial but owner-only.

OR.basis_note: Measure 50: Maximum Assessed Value does NOT reset on sale (investor = owner, ~0.85% of market); BUT major remodel adds exception value at the changed-property ratio - BRRRR rehab partially reassesses.

PA.basis_note: County/school millage on often-stale assessments; Act 1 homestead exclusions are owner-only but modest. Investor ~1.5 of purchase (Philly ~1.4 near-market; Pittsburgh higher on 2012 base).

RI.basis_note: Providence and several cities tax non-owner-occupied residential at materially higher rates / deny 40%+ homestead exemptions -> investor ~1.5-1.65 vs owner ~1.35.

SC.basis_note: 6% ratio (vs 4% owner) AND school operating millage applies (Act 388 exempts only the 4% class) -> ~2.5-3x owner eff (0.5); ATI reassessment to sale price (file 25% ATI exemption by Jan 30 after purchase). Do NOT use the 0.5% homeowner avg.

SD.basis_note: Non-owner-occupied 'other' school GF levy $4.867/1000 vs $0.669 owner-occupied (SB121, payable 2027) -> ~+0.35-0.45pp over owner eff ~1.0.

TN.basis_note: 25% residential ratio for both; no homestead; reappraisal-cycle lag keeps effective-on-purchase ~0.55-0.65.

TX.basis_note: Investor gets NO homestead ($140k school exemption + rate compression are owner-only post-Nov 2025) - full appraised value x total rates ~1.9-2.5% in major metros. Temporary 20%/yr non-homestead appraisal circuit breaker (<=$5M) through 2026. Do NOT use ~1.36% homeowner avg.

UT.basis_note: 45% primary residential exemption APPLIES to long-term rentals (tenant's primary residence, 183+ days; owner files declaration) -> LTR investor ~= owner. Second home/STR pays full value (~1.0%).

VT.basis_note: Statewide NON-homestead education rate $1.703/$100 (FY26, CLA-adjusted to market) + municipal ~0.4-0.5 -> ~2.1% of market. Investor cannot use income-sensitized homestead rate.

VA.basis_note: No homestead; investor = owner; near-market assessments; NoVa ~0.9-1.1, rural lower.

WA.basis_note: No general homestead (senior/disabled only); statutory levy caps; investor = owner ~0.85 of market.

WV.basis_note: Rentals are Class III (outside city, 1.5x Class II max levies) or Class IV (in city, 2x) -> ~2x owner eff (0.5); 60% assessment ratio, values lag market.

WI.basis_note: School levy credit applies to all parcels but lottery credit is primary-residence-only (small); investor ~ owner eff ~1.5.

WY.basis_note: 9.5% ratio x ~65-70 mills; 25% owner-occupied exemption (2025-26) is owner-only, so investor pays full: ~0.62 vs owner ~0.55.
